items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: John Coltrane’s quartet with McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones

ctx.x: Can I guess that your parents looked askance at a music career?

Good guess. Oh yeah. I mean no they didn’t want me to have a career as a musician, although I mean they did encourage my interest in music. I mean they paid for music lessons for me for years, and I should tell this story, going back to the Ellington. In 1965 I was just short of my twelfth birthday and I had this neophyte’s interest in jazz. So there was a three day jazz festival in Pittsburgh at the civic arena that George Wein was producing. And Pittsburgh is about an hour or so’s drive from Youngstown. So for…

Strayhorn was from Pittsburgh, as was Earl Hines. So this was kind of a homecoming for both of them. So this was the bill for one night. And I mean that was the night that basically set me on my career path, even though my parents didn’t realize it at the time nor would they have approved if they’d known it, but I mean that really set me on my career path I mean as far as solidifying a serious interest in jazz. Up to that point I’d been doing my best to listen to top 40 radio to conform to the interest of my…
